EOS bodies write EXIF Orientation from the orientation sensor only when Auto Rotate is on; CameraInfo always records the sensor (horizontal / 90 CW / 270 CW). A Normal EXIF value next to a rotated sensor field is the camera's choice (Auto Rotate off, or the camera pointing straight up or down for copy work). The sensor field is used when EXIF Orientation is missing or invalid (EOS 40D and EOS-1D Mark III files can carry 0), or when the recorded Auto Rotate setting is on.
EasyShare KDC files keep Orientation 1 in their own IFDs; the camera writes the orientation sensor into the EXIF block of its embedded full-size JPEG.
Nikon's own software saves a user rotation in the NEF edit record (MakerNote 0x0E01, rotation in degrees) and re-renders the embedded previews, leaving EXIF Orientation at Normal.
